We are asked to find a Costas array of order 10. A Costas array is a permutation matrix of size n x n where the displacement vectors between any two marks are distinct. Specifically, for a permutation f: {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} (or 1..n depending on convention), we consider all pairs (i, f(i)) and (j, f(j)) with i < j. The displacement vector is (j-i, f(j)-f(i)). The condition is that all such vectors (with j-i > 0) must be distinct. Actually the standard definition: A Costas array is an n x n grid with one dot per row and column, such that the vectors between any two dots are all distinct. Usually the vectors are (dx, dy) with dx>0, or sometimes any dx != 0. The standard condition: For all pairs (i, j) and (k, l) with i < j and k < l, the vectors (j-i, f(j)-f(i)) and (l-k, f(l)-f(k)) are equal only if i=k and j=l. That means no two pairs have the same distance vector (dx, dy). Note that dx > 0 always. dy can be positive, negative, or zero?
